## What We Did

Learned about the Coefficient of Variation and how to use it to assess the reliability of estimates. We also explored the `ggplot2` package in R for creating visualizations of our data.

## Key Concepts

Coefficient of Variation: relative measure of uncertainty; (std. err / estimate) * 100
- under 15%: reliable
- under 30: moderately reliable
- over 30: unreliable
Within tidycensus:
moe_sum() - sum of MOEs
moe_prop() - proportion of MOEs
moe_ratio() - ratio of MOEs

Change over time - watch out for overlapping ACS intervals

ggplot(data) - creates a blank canvas
aes(...) - aesthetic mappings (x, y, color, etc.)
geom_*() - the type of chart, visual components
ex: ggplot(tractdata) + aes(x = population, y = moe_pct) + geom_point()

geom_histogram() - histogram
geom_point() - scatterplot
geom_boxplot() - boxplot
geom_col() - bar chart
geom_line() - line chart
geom_errorbar() - error bars

other useful chart features:
coord_flip() - horizontal graph
slice_head(n = ...) - show only the first few rows of data
str_remove(var, "pattern") - remove text in labels

## Reflection

As someone who has used R significantly in the past, I was already familiar with ggplot2 and its syntax. However, I learned a lot about the Coefficient of Variation and how to use it to assess the reliability of estimates. I would like to explore more the ways in which more granular data can be obtained and how to properly analyze it without introducing too much uncertainty.
